Also test isUriFragmentWithNoContext static method via reflection maybe (private). Could use reflection to call private static method.

Test uriRefersToSubschema static: also private static; we can use reflection.

Test findLexicalRoot: Build a parent chain with hasId flags.

Test findAncestor: same.

Test getRefSchemaNode: Provide a schema node with a $ref? It uses findAncestor().getSchemaNode() and metaSchema.getNodeByFragmentRef etc. We'll stub metaSchema to return node.

Simplify: Create JsonSchema with mocked ValidationContext and simple schema node (ObjectNode). For getRefSchemaNode, we can test JSON pointer resolution. Provide a root schema node with a child "foo": {"type":"string"} and test ref "#/foo". The method will call schemaNode.at("/foo") after decoding. The metaSchema is used only if ref doesn't start with "/". So we can test pointer case.

We need to create JsonSchema instance: Use JsonSchema.from(validationContext, "#", baseUri, schemaNode, null, false). That static method returns new JsonSchema.

Now stub validationContext: create a mock using Mockito.

Set up: when(validationContext.getMetaSchema()).thenReturn(metaSchemaMock); when(validationContext.getConfig()).thenReturn(configMock); when(validationContext.resolveSchemaId(any(JsonNode.class))).thenReturn(null); when(validationContext.getURIFactory()).thenReturn(uriFactoryMock); etc.

For validator creation: when(validationContext.newValidator(anyString(), anyString(), any(JsonNode.class), any(JsonSchema.class), anyString())).thenReturn(mock(JsonValidator.class));

Now test getValidators behavior: call jsonSchema.getValidators() indirectly via reflection maybe not public. getValidators is private; but we can call jsonSchema.validate with empty validators? Actually getValidators is private but used inside validate. For test we can call jsonSchema.validate(node) and ensure no errors.

But we need to test hasRequiredValidator etc. Since schema node may contain "required": ["a"]; then read will create requiredValidator from validationContext.newValidator; but we can check jsonSchema.hasRequiredValidator() true.

Similarly typeValidator.

We'll create schema node with "required": [] and "type": "object". Use Jackson's ObjectMapper to parse.

Now test initializeValidators: ensure validator.preloadJsonSchema called.

We need to verify that after calling initializeValidators, the flag validatorsLoaded becomes true (via reflection) and preload invoked.

Test isDynamicAnchor: set "$recursiveAnchor": true in schema node, ensure dynamicAnchor true.

Test toString returns proper format.

Test createExecutionContext returns ExecutionContext with collector context.

We may need to verify ExecutionContext class exists.
